name: Thomas Massie
role: US Representative from Kentucky (2012–present; lost the May 2026 Republican primary)
summary: Massie is a libertarian-leaning Republican who opposes spending increases and debt, wants to abolish the Federal Reserve, and opposes warrantless surveillance, foreign aid and military interventions. He is a Second Amendment advocate and holds pro-life views on abortion. He often casts lone dissenting votes and has broken with party leadership and Donald Trump. He lost the May 2026 Republican primary to the Trump-endorsed Ed Gallrein.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Supports repealing the Affordable Care Act and replacing federal health programs with a free market; opposed Republican replacement efforts as insufficient.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: He explains that market prices guide cattle production and opposes artificial price suppression.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: He advocates abolishing federal income taxation altogether, rather than increasing its rates.

surveillance-ok.rationale: Floor statement: government should not search Section 702 data on US persons without a warrant; Surveillance State Repeal Act (2015) to repeal the PATRIOT Act and FISA Amendments Act; has called for Snowden pardon.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: Lone vote against H.Res.1125 (2022), saying in his own post that 'government can't legislate thought' and that the resolution 'promoted internet censorship and violations of the 1st amendment'; voted against the 2024 Antisemitism Awareness Act (H.R.6090). Votes on specific measures, so medium.

strong-leader.rationale: No recorded position found: the evidence found addresses a nearby question, not this statement.

limit-guns.rationale: Says weapon bans and gun-free zones are unconstitutional; introduced a bill to repeal the Gun-Free School Zones Act; voted against universal background checks (2019).

decide-locally.rationale: His explicit policy tests favour state and local action and return school decisions to parents and boards.

rehabilitation.rationale: Voted for the FIRST STEP Act in May 2018 and its final version in December 2018, which created recidivism-reduction programmes; also opposes mandatory minimums. Votes for one bill, no stated view on what prisons are for, so low.

abortion-legal.rationale: Called Roe v. Wade a judicial travesty, believes life begins at conception, supports a 20-week ban and voted against the Women's Health Protection Act (2022).

reduce-immigration.rationale: Mixed votes: for the Fairness for High-Skilled Immigrants Act (2019, lifts per-country green-card caps), against the Farm Workforce Modernization Act (2019, expands farmworker visas) and against the 2023 Secure the Border Act. No stated position on overall immigration levels.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: He explicitly offers to sponsor withdrawal from the United Nations.

nation-first.rationale: Describes his opposition to Israel aid as putting America first; no general statement about global cooperation.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Opposes regulating greenhouse gases and cap-and-trade, says the "jury is still out" on human contribution to climate change, supports dismantling the EPA.

expand-nuclear.rationale: 2014 House hearing: he calls Kentucky's moratorium on new nuclear plants wrong and says he is convinced the safety issue is solved, but also says the waste problem must be solved; he does not call for expansion as such.

tax-inheritance.rationale: Voted for the Death Tax Repeal Act (H.R.1105, April 2015), which abolishes the federal estate tax outright. A vote on a bill, so medium.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: March 2025 interview: he would rather fund government with broad, low tariffs than an income tax and says taxing imports discourages buying them, but rejects tariffs that let the executive pick winners and losers; revenue rather than protection, so mixed.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: Introduced the Federal Reserve Board Abolition Act (H.R. 8421 in 2024; reintroduced 2025) and said "the most effective policy is to end the Federal Reserve", blaming it for inflation.

unbreakable-encryption.rationale: His 2015 amendment barred NSA and CIA from requiring backdoors in commercial products.

results-over-ideology.rationale: No recorded position found: the evidence found addresses a nearby question, not this statement.

school-vouchers.rationale: Voted for the SOAR Reauthorization Act (H.R.10, October 2015), which renews the D.C. Opportunity Scholarship voucher programme for private schools. A vote on one programme, so medium and +1.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: Opposes federal stimulus spending and votes against spending bills that add to the debt (CARES Act process 2020, 2025 reconciliation bill, "Debt Badge"); calls spending, not tax cuts, what must be paid for.

work-for-welfare.rationale: In his May 2025 interview he says there is no excuse for able-bodied Medicaid recipients without children not to work and backs those requirements; this covers Medicaid only, not welfare benefits generally.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Voted to approve Keystone XL (2013), for the Offshore Energy and Jobs Act opening offshore leasing (2013) and to overturn the Stream Protection Rule on coal mining (2017). Consistent votes, but votes only, so medium.

separated-powers.rationale: Congressional Record 4 March 2026: he cites Madison and says the Constitution gives Congress the power to initiate war and the President the power to wage it; a war-powers case, not a general statement of checks among all bodies.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: He rejects government attempts to suppress high beef prices rather than address supply.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: He expressly defends members voting their conscience against demands for complete party compliance.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: No recorded position found: the evidence found addresses a nearby question, not this statement.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: No stated position on presidential re-election limits; congressional term limits are something nearby.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: His 9 December 2025 NATO Act press release: he sponsors withdrawal from NATO and says the Constitution did not authorize permanent foreign entanglements; troops abroad and other alliances are not addressed.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: Consistently votes against foreign aid, saying it is paid through inflation and taxes on Americans and objecting to aid commitments.

collective-defense.rationale: He rejects the continuing NATO obligation to act as wealthy allies’ security blanket.

flat-income-tax.rationale: Stated support for a single-rate tax system (2010) and the FairTax; in 2017 wanted to eliminate all deductions. Not a precise endorsement of a flat income tax.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: No recorded position found: the evidence found addresses a nearby question, not this statement.

no-bailouts.rationale: No recorded position found: the evidence found addresses a nearby question, not this statement.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: Congressional Record 10 June 2015: he invokes the Fourth Amendment as requiring a warrant and says intelligence agencies are not above it; a single amendment, not a general case for entrenched rights.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: April 2026 Senate hearing: the Second Amendment is for defence 'not only from a lone assailant, but from the whole of tyrannical government', warning of 'a corrupt and dangerous few' who 'attempt to subjugate the masses'. Speaks to resisting tyranny in general, not to lawfully removing a ruler, and reported secondhand, so low.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: The earlier answer rested only on an OnTheIssues listing taken from an interest-group rating (2012); no vote, bill or statement of his on Social Security personal accounts found.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: No recorded position found: the evidence found addresses a nearby question, not this statement.

corporate-influence.rationale: CNN 2 September 2026: he says a Brazilian meatpacker's inauguration donation bought access and money is buying an outcome against farmers; one case, not a general statement.

non-intervention.rationale: Re-checked under rules 3: the earlier answer cited only Wikipedia. His own words oppose particular interventions (Venezuela, Iran) on war-powers grounds and say Congress should vote if military action is justified, which does not reach 'for any reason'. No stated position on the statement as worded.

public-access-to-information.rationale: Sponsored the Epstein Files Transparency Act (H.R.4405) requiring the Justice Department to publish its Epstein files, and voted for it (2025). A specific disclosure law, not a stated general right of access, so low.

national-law-over-international.rationale: He rejects WTO adjudication above the US Supreme Court and constitution.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: Same NATO release: sponsors leaving one alliance and rejects permanent entanglements; neutrality between rival blocs is not stated.

promulgated-standing-laws.rationale: No recorded position found: the evidence found addresses a nearby question, not this statement.

term-limits.rationale: Supports a constitutional amendment for congressional term limits (2017).

abolish-ip.rationale: Says he supports intellectual property protections as necessary for innovation, noting this is an area where he is not a libertarian.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: Calls self-defense a right guaranteed in the Constitution and says 'the only thing that stops a bad guy with a gun is a good guy with a gun' (2017 statement); told a Senate hearing in April 2026 that the Second Amendment exists 'for the defense of one's home, one's family, and one's community'. Quoted in press reports, so medium.

anonymous-payments.rationale: Voted for the CBDC Anti-Surveillance State Act (H.R.5403, 2024), which bars a central bank digital currency the government could use to surveil transactions. A vote on one bill, not a stated view on untraceable payments generally, so low.

regional-powers-revocable.rationale: No recorded position found: the evidence found addresses a nearby question, not this statement.

state-arms-monopoly.rationale: Treats the right to bear arms as God-given and opposes limits on gun ownership, which conflicts with reserving arms to the state.

fiscal-rules-binding.rationale: Voted for the balanced budget amendment H.J.Res.139 (March 2026) but against H.J.Res.2 (April 2018); the most recent vote is for a binding constitutional rule. Votes only, one each way, so low.

public-service-media.rationale: He advocates legislative rescissions cutting NPR and PBS subsidies.

mandatory-sentences.rationale: He opposes mandatory minimums because judges and juries should retain sentencing discretion.

indirect-election.rationale: March 2025 interview: he would 'repeal the year 1913', including the 17th Amendment 'which allowed direct election of senators', calling direct election of senators and direct taxation 'really dangerous to this country, injurious to our Republic'. Favours senators chosen by state legislatures; spoken about the Senate only, so medium.

no-business-privileges.rationale: He objects to corporate energy subsidies and tax preferences benefiting lobby-backed firms over individuals.

notes:
Many answers rest on aggregator or news summaries of his votes; his House issue pages were not reachable at guessed URLs. Not answered for lack of a stated position on the statement as worded: tariffs and free trade (sources conflict: sugar tariffs sponsored in 2013, later reported opposition to Trump tariffs not verified in an opened page), recreational drug legalization (supports hemp and medical cannabis), same-sex marriage, Israel statehood, war powers principles beyond opposing specific wars.

Merged with an independent gpt-6.1-sol audit: 28 answers taken from it, 12 agreed, 0 conflicts settled by the integrator.

gpt-6.1-sol notes: Independent pass under the October 28 source-priority rules. Existing notes and sources only were consulted; no existing answers copied, and no living-person inference used. Full original interviews, congressional passages and official releases were checked across all 490 statements, including remaining nulls. Rhetoric is medium or lower. The March 2025 interview is available in full in the publisher’s public magazine PDF, although its separate webpage is paywalled. The June 2025 public interview PDF was opened through web after direct download failed. Ratings and interviewer opinions are excluded. The privacy amendment contains exceptions for lawful surveillance and telecommunications mandates, hence qualified answers rather than a claim he rejects every warrant or requires mathematically unbreakable systems. His NATO withdrawal bill explicitly rejects permanent foreign entanglements; UN withdrawal is kept distinct from a military treaty. His endorsement of broad low revenue tariffs in place of income taxation is distinguished from selective protection of favoured industries. Opposition to a particular war does not establish an exceptionless non-intervention or defensive-war-only doctrine. The anti-abortion statement addresses legal protection of unborn life, not merely attendance at a march; the 2025 bill confirms continuity. A 2012 signed term-limit pledge is an institutional amendment pledge, not a promise to leave after three terms before such an amendment exists. Personal off-grid living and family preferences are not converted into cultural prescriptions; no specific culture statement established. Vote-by-mail objections do not justify presidential lawmaking in his stated view. No same-sex-marriage legality inferred solely from opposition to federal codification.
